title: Query Registry
summary: Query registry is the reading of the Windows registry to learn how a host is built, configured and protected. The registry holds operating system settings, installed software, security policy, service configuration and traces of past user activity, so a handful of reads answers questions that would otherwise need many separate commands. The Reg utility is the classic method, but the same values are reachable through PowerShell, the command shell, Windows Management Instrumentation, native application programming interface calls, and by parsing a copy of a hive taken from disk. Because reads change nothing, the behaviour is quiet; it is most visible in process creation telemetry where command lines such as reg query appear, in script block logging, and in registry auditing when a system access control list has been set on a key worth watching. Administrators and inventory agents read the same keys constantly, so the useful discriminators are which keys were touched, by which account, how often, whether the reads were scripted in a loop, and whether they cluster with other discovery on that host.

beginner.definition: The registry is a large store of settings inside Windows. Query registry means reading those settings to learn about a computer. An attacker looks for installed software, security settings and traces of user activity. Reading the registry does not change it, so the computer keeps working exactly as before.
beginner.whyItMatters: The registry answers many questions at once, so an attacker can plan quickly. It can show which security product is installed, which accounts exist, and what starts when the machine boots. The reads are quiet and need no extra tool, because Windows ships with the commands. Without logging, you may only notice the attack after it has moved on.
howItWorks: The attacker opens a shell or script on the machine they already control.
They run built-in commands that read chosen registry keys and their values.
They look for security products, such as antivirus, logging and endpoint agents.
They read settings that list installed software, running services and startup programs.
They also check network and account settings to plan their next step.
They may repeat the reads on other machines to build a picture of the estate.
beginner.example: Think of a caretaker's office in a school. On the wall hangs a folder listing every room, every key, and every alarm code. A visitor who reads that folder learns which door has no alarm and where the master key is kept. They touch nothing and leave no mark on any room. Query registry is that folder. It is a read only visit, and the building looks exactly the same afterwards.
takeaways: Registry reads are quiet, so process and command line logging is your main evidence.
Attacks often query keys that list security tools before they act.
Auditing a few high value keys can turn a silent read into a visible event.

objectives: Describe the kinds of information an attacker can obtain by reading the Windows registry.
Name several ways the registry can be queried besides the Reg utility.
Explain why registry queries are difficult to detect without process telemetry.
Identify registry keys worth auditing because they reveal security posture.
Distinguish routine administrative queries from reconnaissance behaviour.
